samples.text:
The chart shows how many people visited a national park in the four seasons in 2021, 2022 and 2023.

Summer was the most popular season in all three years. In 2021 there was 210,000 visitors, and it went up to 260,000 in 2022. However, in 2023 it decreased a little bit to 245,000. Autumn was the second popular season. It had 120,000 visitors in 2021 and 115,000 in 2022, then it rose to 150,000 in 2023.

Spring visitors increased every year. It started at 85,000 in 2021 and rose to 110,000 in 2022 and 140,000 in 2023. Winter was the least popular season, but the number of visitors also grow each year, from 30,000 to 45,000 and then 70,000, so it more than doubled in this period.

Overall, summer had the most visitors and winter had the fewest in all years. The number of visitors in spring and winter increased steady, while in summer and autumn the numbers went up and down.
samples.why: Accurate figures, all seasons covered · overview placed at the end · simple, repetitive linking · adequate vocabulary, some informal phrasing · agreement, word-form and tense errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The bar chart compares the number of visitors to a national park in spring, summer, autumn and winter over a three-year period from 2021 to 2023.

Overall, summer was consistently the busiest season, while winter attracted the fewest visitors. Numbers in spring and winter increased steadily each year, whereas summer and autumn showed less regular patterns. In total, the park received more visitors in each successive year.

Summer visitor numbers rose from 210,000 in 2021 to a peak of 260,000 in 2022, before falling slightly to 245,000 in the final year. Autumn, which was the second busiest season in all three years, saw a small drop from 120,000 to 115,000, followed by significant rise to 150,000 in 2023.

Spring showed the most consistent growth. The number of visitors increased from 85,000 to 110,000 and then to 140,000, meaning that spring had almost caught up with autumn by the end of the period. Although winter remained the quietest season, visitor numbers more than doubled over the three years, climbing from 30,000 to 45,000 and eventually reaching 70,000.
samples.why: Clear overview of peak, low and trends · key features well highlighted · logical progression and a range of cohesive devices · some less common vocabulary · generally accurate grammar with one article slip.

samples.text:
The chart illustrates seasonal visitor numbers at a national park over three consecutive years, from 2021 to 2023.

Summer was the park's peak season throughout, and winter the quietest. Overall, however, the park became busier over the period, with the most sustained growth occurring in spring and winter, the two seasons that increased year on year.

Summer attracted the largest numbers by a wide margin, rising from 210,000 visitors in 2021 to 260,000 the following year, before easing slightly to 245,000 in 2023; this was the only season to record a fall in the final year. Autumn followed an almost opposite pattern: after a marginal dip from 120,000 to 115,000, it rose sharply to 150,000, its highest level in the period.

Spring, meanwhile, grew steadily from 85,000 to 110,000 and then 140,000, an overall increase of 55,000 that brought it within striking distance of the autumn figure. Although winter remained by far the least popular season, it showed the strongest relative growth, with visitor numbers more than doubling from 30,000 to 70,000 over the two years, via 45,000 in 2022.
samples.why: Key features skilfully selected with a clear overview · figures used selectively, including accurate derived growth · cohesion managed skilfully · wide, precise vocabulary · varied, error-free structures.
